elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative language expressly permits Customer to terminate “this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its convenience-termination right on 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The added language requires “thirty days' prior” notice.

elements.element: Customer's convenience-termination notice must be written and directed to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The added language specifies “written notice to Vendor.”

elements.element: Vendor must refund prepaid fees following Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The added language states that “Vendor shall refund prepaid fees.”

elements.element: The refund must be calculated pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: The added language requires a refund “pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly states that Vendor has no such right “during a committed term.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added operative language expressly grants Customer this convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only 30 days' prior notice, which is below the fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed by the rendered clause, so the conditional cap is not triggered and is not exceeded.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause does not grant Vendor an affirmative convenience-termination right; it instead denies such a right during a committed term.

elements.element: Any Vendor convenience-termination right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor convenience-termination right is granted, so the condition for exercising such a right is demonstrably absent; the clause also expressly bars such termination during a committed term.

elements.element: Any Vendor convenience termination requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No Vendor convenience-termination right is granted, so the notice condition is not triggered. The fallback nevertheless fails because the required affirmative Vendor right is absent.

result.reason: The operative addition fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives a 30-day written convenience-termination right, a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and Vendor is barred from convenience termination during a committed term. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because Customer's notice period is only 30 days and Vendor receives no affirmative end-of-term convenience right. The change is substantively focused and does not disturb the existing for-cause rights, but drafting quality is reduced because the new provision is unnumbered and appears after Section 9.5 even though the open Section 9.4 slot is available, and “committed term” is not defined in the supplied language.
